intro.label: Before Puppy Comes Home
intro.heading: What do you need before bringing home a Gordon Setter puppy?
intro.html:
Before your Gordon Setter puppy arrives, three priorities: verify you have all health documentation from the breeder, learn the signs of bloat/GDV and locate your nearest 24-hour emergency vet, and start a grooming habituation plan. The GDV piece sounds alarmist but it's practical preparation — knowing where to drive at 11pm when your dog is in distress is not something to figure out in the moment.

Documentation Checklist (Get from Breeder)

  • OFA hip clearances for both parents
  • OFA thyroid clearances for both parents
  • CAER eye exam results for both parents
  • PRA DNA test results for both parents
  • Puppy's vaccination and deworming records
  • Microchip number (if done by breeder)

Gear Checklist

  • Crate (36–42 inch depending on expected adult size, with divider panel)
  • Orthopedic dog bed
    One option: Bedsure Orthopedic Bolster Dog Bed (XL, 42 x 32 in) on Amazon. A bolstered bed with egg-crate foam, a low entry, and a removable machine-washable cover with a waterproof layer. Check the size chart (this is the XL, 42 x 32 in size); it's egg-crate foam rather than memory foam.
  • Stainless steel food and water bowls
  • Flat collar + ID tag — engrave before arrival
    One option: GoTags Personalized Stainless Steel ID Tag on Amazon. An engraved stainless steel ID tag; you pick the shape and the lines of text at checkout. Put a phone number that's actually answered on it, and update the engraving if you move.
  • Harness for walks
  • 4–6 ft leash
    One option: Joytale Double-Handle Leash (6 ft) on Amazon. A 6-foot nylon leash with a padded second handle near the clip for close control, plus reflective stitching for dark walks. The 1-inch webbing suits medium and large dogs; it can feel heavy on a young puppy.
  • Slicker brush and wide-tooth steel comb — start grooming habituation from day one
    One option: Chris Christensen Big G Slicker Brush on Amazon. The Big G has long, angled pins set in a flexible cushioned pad, built for working through double, long and curly coats. Use light strokes; slicker pins can scratch skin if pressed hard.
  • Dog-safe shampoo and conditioner (silky coat formula)
  • Ear cleaning solution and cotton balls
  • High-value training treats
    One option: Blue Buffalo Bits Soft Training Treats, Beef (19 oz) on Amazon. Soft, bite-size training treats with real beef as the first ingredient, small enough for rapid repetitions. Keep treats to about 10% of daily calories.
  • Enzymatic cleaner
    One option: Nature's Miracle Dog Stain & Odor Remover (32 oz) on Amazon. An enzymatic stain and odor cleaner that keeps breaking down urine and other organic messes after you apply it. Spot-test on carpet or upholstery first.

care.label: First Week Setup
care.heading: What should the first week with a Gordon Setter puppy look like?
care.html:
First Vet Visit (Within 48–72 Hours)

  • Full physical exam and vaccine continuation
  • Parasite prevention appropriate for your region
  • Discuss gastropexy — ask your vet's recommendation on preventive gastropexy during spay/neuter. This is a $300–$500 add-on that significantly reduces GDV risk. Have this conversation now, not the day of surgery.
  • Microchip if not done by breeder
  • Enroll in pet insurance before or immediately after this visit — before any conditions are documented

Know the Signs of Bloat/GDV Before You Need To

GDV is a life-threatening emergency with a tight time window. Know these signs:

  • Distended, bloated-looking abdomen (especially after eating)
  • Unproductive retching — the dog tries to vomit but nothing comes up
  • Excessive drooling
  • Restlessness, inability to get comfortable
  • Pale gums

If you see these signs, go to an emergency vet immediately — do not wait to see if it gets better. Program the nearest 24-hour emergency veterinary clinic into your phone now, before you need it. This is not an overreaction; it's practical preparation for a real risk.

Start Grooming Habituation From Day One

  • Daily brief brushing sessions — not for coat management yet, but for habituation
  • Ear handling at every session — flip ears back, look inside, touch the outer canal
  • Paw handling — manipulate each toe, simulate nail trimming
  • Mouth handling — open gently, touch gums

A Gordon Setter that was handled throughout puppyhood accepts grooming easily as an adult. One that wasn't becomes increasingly resistant as their size and strength grows.

special.label: Training and Management
special.heading: Building Good Habits Through the Long Adolescence
special.html:
Patience Through Slow Maturation

Gordon Setters mature slowly — mentally, many dogs remain in an adolescent phase until age 2–3. Establish consistent training from the start and maintain it through the adolescent period, even when it feels like the dog has forgotten everything they learned at 12 weeks. Consistency during the adolescence pays off in the settled, devoted adult.

  • Sit, down, stay, come, leave it — establish and proof consistently from puppyhood
  • Loose-leash walking — start from the first walk, never allow pulling to become habitual
  • Door manners and threshold behavior — sit before going outside, wait at thresholds
  • Recall training — invest in this specifically. A sporting dog in an interesting environment has competing priorities; reliable recall requires real training investment.

Socialization

Gordon Setters are more reserved with strangers than Irish Setters — early socialization is important for a well-adjusted adult. During the critical window (8–16 weeks):

  • Varied people: different ages, appearances, uniforms, hats
  • Varied environments: traffic, crowds, different surfaces and sounds
  • Positive interactions with strangers that the puppy initiates at their own pace — don't force greeting
  • Puppy class for structured socialization with vaccinated puppies

Exercise Rules for Puppies

5 minutes per month of age, twice daily maximum. Growth plates in a large breed close around 18 months — no forced running, jumping, or stair climbing until then. On-leash walks and free play in a yard are appropriate; jogging with the dog waits until 18 months minimum.

faq.q: What health clearances should a Gordon Setter breeder provide?
faq.a: OFA hip clearances, OFA thyroid clearances, CAER eye exam results, and PRA DNA test results for both parents. Ask for documentation copies, not just verbal assurance. Reputable breeders will have these without hesitation. If a breeder can't produce them, that's a red flag regardless of how nice the puppies look.

faq.q: How do I prepare for bloat/GDV risk in my Gordon Setter?
faq.a: Three steps: (1) Learn the signs — distended abdomen, unproductive retching, restlessness, drooling after eating. (2) Program your nearest 24-hour emergency veterinary clinic into your phone now. (3) Discuss preventive gastropexy with your vet at the first appointment — a $300–$500 procedure during spay/neuter significantly reduces risk. Enroll in pet insurance before the first vet visit to cover emergency surgery costs if needed.

faq.q: Are Gordon Setters harder to train than other sporting breeds?
faq.a: Moderately — they're intelligent and respond well to consistent positive reinforcement, but they mature slowly and can seem to regress during adolescence. They're not stubborn in the way northern breeds are, but they need consistent, patient training through a longer adolescent phase than many breeds. A trainer experienced with sporting dogs is helpful. They are not as immediately biddable as retrievers but are significantly more cooperative than primitive breeds.
